body.translated_text: The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Lady <s>Tārā</s>
Oṃ, homage to the glorious noble <s>Tārā</s>!

children.translated_text: On the glorious <s>Potalaka</s>, delightful, resplendent with various minerals,
filled with various trees and creepers, resounding with the songs of various birds, (verse 1)
with the roaring of various waterfalls, teeming with various animals,
surrounded on all sides by various species of flowers, (verse 2)
endowed with various heart-fruits, resonating with the humming of bees,
with sweet songs of <s>Kinnaras</s>, teeming with intoxicated elephants, (verse 3)
resounding with hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Vidyādharas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: munibhir vītarāgaiś ca satataṃ saṃniṣevite // Tbh_4
children.translated_text: constantly attended by sages free from passion, (verse 4)
and by other hosts of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, lords of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
by <s>Āyatārā</s> and other thousands of goddess-queens of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), (verse 5)
and surrounded by other hosts of wrathful kings, headed by <s>Hayagrīva</s> —
the Blessed <s>Avalokita</s>, devoted to the welfare of all beings, (verse 6)
the glorious one, dwelt there, seated on a lotus-heart throne,

children.text: mahatā tapasā yukto maitryā ca kṛpayānvitaḥ // Tbh_7
children.translated_text: endowed with great austerity, filled with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and compassion. (verse 7)

children.text: dharmaṃ dideśa tasyāṃ sa mahatyāṃ devaparṣadi /
children.translated_text: He taught the <s>Dharma</s> there in that great assembly of gods.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, of great strength, approached the one seated there, (verse 8)
filled with supreme compassion, and asked <s>Avalokita</s> thus:
"In the perils of thieves, serpents, lions, fire, elephants, tigers, and floods, (verse 9)

children.text: sīdanty amī mune satvā magnāḥ saṃsārasāgare /
children.translated_text: these beings are suffering, O sage, drowning in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),
bound by the fetters of <s>saṃsāra</s>, afflicted by passion, hatred, and darkness. (verse 10)

children.text: mucyante yena saṃsārāt tan me brūhi mahāmune /
children.translated_text: By what means are they freed from <s>saṃsāra</s>? Tell me that, O great sage!"

children.text: evam ukte jagannāthaḥ sa śrīmān avalokitaḥ // Tbh_10bis
children.translated_text: When thus addressed, the Lord of the World, the glorious <s>Avalokita</s>, (verse 10bis)
spoke sweet words to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the awakener:
"Listen, O <s>Guhyaka</s>-king, <s>Indra</s>! Born from the power of the vow of <s>Amitābha</s>, the Protector, (verse 11)
by my command, the Mothers of the World,
endowed with great compassion, devoted to the deliverance of the world, (verse 12)
radiant like the risen sun, with faces bright as the full moon,
the <s>Tārās</s> illuminate the trees, along with gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans. (verse 13)
They cause the three worlds to tremble, terrifying <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: nīlotpalakarā devī mā bhair mā bhair iti bruvan // Tbh_14
children.translated_text: the goddess, holding a blue lotus in her hand, says 'Fear not! Fear not!' (verse 14)
For the protection of the world I have been brought forth by the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors).
In the wilderness, in the clash of weapons, in various fearful dangers, (verse 15)

children.text: smaraṇād eva nāmāni satvān rakṣāmy ahaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: by merely remembering my names, I always protect beings.
I shall ferry them across, O Lord, from the great ocean of various fears. (verse 16)

children.text: tena tāreti maṃ loke gāyanti munipuṃgavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore the foremost sages sing of me in the world as '<s>Tārā</s>' (She who ferries across)."
Then, having joined their palms, with respect and awe, (verse 17)
blazing, standing in the sky, he spoke these words:

children.text: nāmāṣṭaśatakaṃ brūhi yat purā kīrtitaṃ jinaiḥ // Tbh_18
children.translated_text: "Speak the one hundred and eight names that were formerly proclaimed by the <s>Jinas</s>, (verse 18)
by the lords of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural power,
which remove all sins, are meritorious, auspicious, and increase fame, (verse 19)
which remove poverty and increase health and prosperity.

children.text: maitrīm ālambya satvānāṃ tat kīrtaya mahāmune // Tbh_20
children.translated_text: Out of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward beings, proclaim them, O great sage!" (verse 20)
When thus addressed, the Blessed <s>Avalokita</s>, smiling,

children.text: vyavalokya diśaḥ sarvā maitryā sphuraṇayā dṛśā // Tbh_21
children.translated_text: surveying all directions with a gaze radiating <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), (verse 21)
raising his right hand, adorned with auspicious marks,

children.text: tam uvāca mahāprājñaḥ sādhu sādhu mahātapaḥ // Tbh_22
children.translated_text: the one of great wisdom spoke to him: "Excellent, excellent, O one of great austerity! (verse 22)
Listen to the names, O greatly fortunate one, who cherishes all beings equally,

children.text: yāni saṃkīrtya manujāḥ samyak te syur dhaneśvarāḥ // Tbh_23
children.translated_text: by fully reciting which, people shall become lords of wealth, (verse 23)
freed from all diseases, endowed with all sovereign qualities,
and those consumed by untimely death, upon passing, shall go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Blissful Realm). (verse 24)

body.text: tāny ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi devasaṃghāḥ śṛṇudhva me

children.translated_text: Rejoice in the true <s>Dharma</s> and become well-liberated! (verse 25)

children.text: oṃ locane sulocane tāre tārotsave sarvasatvānukampini /
children.translated_text: Oṃ! O <s>Locanā</s> (She with Eyes)! O <s>Sulocanā</s> (She with Beautiful Eyes)! O <s>Tārā</s>! O Joy of <s>Tārā</s>! O she who has compassion for all beings!
O Deliverer of all beings! O Thousand-Armed! O Thousand-Eyed! (verse 26)
Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed One! O she who sees! O she who is seen!
And I, for all beings — phuṭ svāhā! (verse 27)
Oṃ! O Pure One! O Perfectly Pure One! O Purifier and Thorough Purifier!

children.text: sugatātmaje maitrīhṛdaye nirmale śyāme śyāmarūpiṇi // Tbh_28
children.translated_text: O Daughter of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone)! O she whose heart is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)! O Stainless One! O Dark One! O she of dark form! (verse 28)
O One of Great Wisdom! O Excellent One! O she adorned with excellence! O Invincible One!
O Greatly Fierce One! O she of universal form! O One of Great Glory! (verse 29)
She whose splendor is like the fire at the end of an age (<s>kalpāgni</s>), she of great glory as the sustainer of the world (<s>lokadhātrī</s>),
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, the wide-eyed one (<s>viśālākṣī</s>), she who increases wisdom, glory, and intellect (<s>prajñāśrībuddhivardhanī</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 30 //

children.text: oṃ dhṛtidā puṣṭidā svāhā oṃkārā kāmarūpiṇī /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, the bestower of steadfastness (<s>dhṛtidā</s>), the bestower of nourishment (<s>puṣṭidā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>, she who is <s>Oṃkāra</s>, she who assumes forms at will (<s>kāmarūpiṇī</s>),
she who is devoted to the welfare of all beings, the deliverer (<s>tāraṇī</s>) in battle, the victorious one (<s>jayā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 31 //
The goddess <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), the noble <s>Tārā</s>, the delightful one (<s>manoramā</s>),
companion of the [dharma-]drum (<s>dundubhisakhinī</s>), the queen of perfect knowledge (<s>pūrṇavidyārājñī</s>), she of pleasing speech (<s>priyaṃvadā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 32 //
Moon-faced (<s>candrānanā</s>), supremely fair (<s>mahāgaurī</s>), unconquered (<s>ajitā</s>), clad in yellow garments (<s>pītavāsas</s>),
the great illusion (<s>mahāmāyā</s>), the great white one (<s>mahāśvetā</s>), she of great strength and valor (<s>mahābalaparākramā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 33 //
The greatly fierce one (<s>mahāraudrī</s>), the greatly wrathful one (<s>mahācaṇḍī</s>), the destroyer of evil beings (<s>duṣṭasatvanisūdanī</s>),

children.text: praśāntā śāntarūpā ca vijayā jvalanaprabhā // Tbh_34
children.translated_text: the peaceful one (<s>praśāntā</s>), she of tranquil form (<s>śāntarūpā</s>), the victorious one (<s>vijayā</s>), she whose radiance is like fire (<s>jvalanaprabhā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 34 //
She who wears a garland of lightning (<s>vidyunmālī</s>), she who bears a banner (<s>dhvajī</s>), a sword (<s>khaḍgī</s>), a discus (<s>cakrī</s>), and a bow with weapons (<s>cāpayutāyudhā</s>),

children.text: jambhanī stambhanī kālī kālarātrī niśācarī // Tbh_35
children.translated_text: she who paralyzes (<s>jambhanī</s>), she who immobilizes (<s>stambhanī</s>), <s>Kālī</s>, the dark night (<s>kālarātrī</s>), she who moves in the night (<s>niśācarī</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 35 //

children.text: rakṣaṇī mohinī śāntā kāntā vibhāvinī śubhā /
children.translated_text: The protectress (<s>rakṣaṇī</s>), the enchantress (<s>mohinī</s>), the peaceful one (<s>śāntā</s>), the beautiful one (<s>kāntā</s>), the radiant one (<s>vibhāvinī</s>), the auspicious one (<s>śubhā</s>),

children.text: brāhmaṇī vedamātā ca guhā ca guhavāsinī // Tbh_36
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, the mother of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>vedamātā</s>), <s>Guhā</s>, and she who dwells in caves (<s>guhavāsinī</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 36 //
The auspicious one (<s>māṅgalyā</s>), the beneficent one (<s>śaṅkarī</s>), the gentle one (<s>saumyā</s>), the sacred fire (<s>jātavedā</s>), she who is swift as thought (<s>manojavā</s>),
the skull-bearer (<s>kāpālinī</s>), the greatly fortunate one (<s>mahābhāgā</s>), twilight (<s>saṃdhyā</s>), truth (<s>satyā</s>), the unconquered one (<s>aparājitā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 37 //
The caravan-leader (<s>sārthavāhā</s>), she of compassionate gaze (<s>kṛpādṛṣṭī</s>), she who shows the way to those who have lost it (<s>naṣṭamārgapradarśanī</s>),
the boon-granter (<s>varadā</s>), the instructor (<s>śāsanī</s>), the teacher (<s>śāstrī</s>), she who has a feminine form with immeasurable valor (<s>strīrūpāmitavikramā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 38 //

children.text: śavalī yoginī siddhā cāṇḍālī cāmṛtā dhruvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śavalī</s>, the <s>yoginī</s>, the perfected one (<s>siddhā</s>), the <s>caṇḍālī</s>, the immortal one (<s>amṛtā</s>), the steadfast one (<s>dhruvā</s>),

children.text: dhanyā puṇyā mahābhāgā subhāgā priyadarśanī // Tbh_39
children.translated_text: the blessed one (<s>dhanyā</s>), the meritorious one (<s>puṇyā</s>), the greatly fortunate one (<s>mahābhāgā</s>), the well-favored one (<s>subhāgā</s>), she of pleasing appearance (<s>priyadarśanī</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 39 //
She who terrifies Death (<s>kṛtāntatrāsanī</s>), the terrifying one (<s>bhīmā</s>), the fierce one (<s>ugrā</s>), she of fierce and great austerity (<s>ugramahātapā</s>),
she who is devoted solely to the welfare of the world, the refuge (<s>śaraṇyā</s>), she who is affectionate to her devotees (<s>bhaktivatsalā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 40 //

The mistress of speech (<s>vāgīśvarī</s>), the auspicious one (<s>śivā</s>), the subtle one (<s>sūkṣmā</s>), the eternal one (<s>nityā</s>), the mother-syllabary of all purposes (<s>sarvārthamātṛkā</s>),

children.text: sarvārthasādhanī bhadrā goptrī dhātrī dhanaṃjayā // Tbh_41
children.translated_text: the accomplisher of all aims (<s>sarvārthasādhanī</s>), the gracious one (<s>bhadrā</s>), the protectress (<s>goptrī</s>), the sustainer (<s>dhātrī</s>), the conqueror of wealth (<s>dhanaṃjayā</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 41 //
The fearless one (<s>abhayā</s>), <s>Gautamī</s>, the meritorious one (<s>puṇyā</s>), the glorious daughter of <s>Lokeśvara</s>,
<s>Tārā</s>, whose names and virtues are endless, the fulfiller of all wishes (<s>sarvāśāparipūraṇī</s>). // <s>Tbh</s> 42 //
This hymn of one hundred and eight names has been proclaimed for your benefit;

children.text: rahasyam adbhutaṃ guhyaṃ devānām api durlabham / 43
children.translated_text: it is secret, wondrous, hidden, and rare even for the gods. // 43 //
It brings good fortune, creates prosperity, and destroys all sins;
it pacifies all diseases and brings happiness to all beings. // <s>Tbh</s> 44 //

children.text: trikāraṃ yaḥ paṭhed dhīmān śuciḥ snānasamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise person who recites it three times, being pure and composed after bathing,
will within a short time attain the splendor of sovereignty. // <s>Tbh</s> 45 //

children.text: duḥkhitaḥ syāt sukhī nityadaridro dhanavān bhavet /
children.translated_text: One who is miserable will become happy, one who is always poor will become wealthy,

children.text: jaḍo bhaven mahāprājño medhāvī ca na saṃśayaḥ // Tbh_46
children.translated_text: one who is dull will become greatly wise and intelligent — there is no doubt. // <s>Tbh</s> 46 //

children.text: bandhanān mucyate baddho vyavahāre jayo bhavet /
children.translated_text: One who is bound will be released from bondage, in lawsuits there will be victory,

children.text: śatravo mitratāṃ yānti śṛṅgiṇaś cātha daṃṣṭriṇaḥ // Tbh_47
children.translated_text: enemies will become friends, as will horned [beasts] and fanged [creatures]. // <s>Tbh</s> 47 //
In battle, in distress, in fortresses, beset by manifold dangers,

children.text: smaraṇād eva nāmāni sarvapāpāny apohati // Tbh_48
children.translated_text: by the mere remembrance of [these] names, all sins are removed. // <s>Tbh</s> 48 //
There will be no untimely death, and one attains abundant prosperity;

children.text: mānuśyaṃ saphalaṃ janma yasya kasya mahātmanaḥ // Tbh_49
children.translated_text: fruitful will be the human birth of whatever great soul [recites this]. // <s>Tbh</s> 49 //

children.text: yaś cedaṃ prātar utthāya mānavaḥ kīrtayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: Whoever, rising at dawn, will recite this,

children.text: sa dīrghakālam āyuṣmān śriyaṃ ca labhate naraḥ // Tbh_50
children.translated_text: that person will be long-lived and will obtain prosperity. // <s>Tbh</s> 50 //

children.text: devā nāgās tathā yakṣā gandharvāḥ kaṭapūtanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods (<s>devas</s>), <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>,
<s>piśācas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>mātṛs</s> (mothers) of fierce splendor, // <s>Tbh</s> 51 //
those who cause consumption and epilepsy, as well as <s>kṣatakākhorḍakas</s> and the like,

children.text: ḍākinyās tārakā pretāḥ skandā mārā mahāgrahāḥ // Tbh_52
children.translated_text: <s>ḍākinīs</s>, <s>tārakās</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>skandas</s>, <s>māras</s>, great seizers (<s>mahāgraha</s>) — // <s>Tbh</s> 52 //

children.text: chāyām api na laṅghante kiṃ punas tasya vigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: they cannot even cross [that person's] shadow, much less [harm] that person's body;

children.text: duṣṭasatvā na vādhante vyādhayo nākramanti ca // Tbh_53
children.translated_text: evil beings do not afflict [them], nor do diseases assail [them]. // <s>Tbh</s> 53 //
They experience even battles between gods and <s>asuras</s>, possessed of great supernatural powers;

children.text: sarvaiśvaryaguṇair yuktaḥ putrapautraiś ca vardhate // Tbh_54
children.translated_text: endowed with all lordly qualities, one prospers with sons and grandsons. // <s>Tbh</s> 54 //

children.text: jātismaro bhaved dhīmān kulīnaḥ priyadarśanaḥ // Tbh_55
children.translated_text: One becomes wise with memory of past births (<s>jātismara</s>), noble-born, and of pleasing appearance. // <s>Tbh</s> 55 //
One becomes joyful, a great orator, and skilled in all <s>śāstras</s> (treatises). // <s>Tbh</s> 56 //
One who associates with virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), adorned with the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>),
will never be separated from <s>Buddhas</s>, wherever one is reborn. // <s>Tbh</s> 57 //

body.translated_text: I shall now proclaim them — O hosts of gods, listen to me!
Thus concludes the Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Lady <s>Tārā</s> (<s>Āryatārābhaṭṭārikā</s>), spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>.
